subject: B2 Creative Arts
figureLabel: Exploring ideas from local people and history
altText: Basic 2 learners in Ghana looking at photos and drawings of elders, farmers, traders and local heroes on a classroom wall.
detailedDescription: In a Basic 2 classroom, a Ghanaian teacher has pinned photographs and drawings of elders, farmers, market women, health workers and local heroes on a display board. Small groups of learners stand nearby, pointing and talking about who these people are, what they do and what they admire about them. Some children make quick sketches in their sketchbooks. The scene shows pupils using people and stories from their community as rich visual ideas for new artworks.

subject: B2 Creative Arts
figureLabel: Observing buildings and artworks as visual ideas
altText: Basic 2 pupils sketching nearby buildings, signboards, murals and decorated objects outside their school.
detailedDescription: Outside the classroom, Basic 2 learners sit and stand where they can see important buildings and artworks in their locality: a small church or mosque, a kiosk with a hand-painted sign, a wall mural and decorated pots. Some pupils sketch doorways, windows and roofs, while others draw patterns from the signboard or pots. The teacher encourages them to look closely at shapes, patterns and colours and to talk about what they see.

subject: B2 Creative Arts
figureLabel: Using environment and topical issues as art ideas
altText: Basic 2 pupils observing a choked gutter, a clean compound and a road crossing while discussing art ideas.
detailedDescription: Near the school, a teacher guides Basic 2 learners to observe real scenes: a dirty gutter filled with rubbish, a clean swept compound with dustbins and a busy road crossing. Learners point, talk about what they notice and suggest how art can help teach people to change. Some sketch quick ideas for posters. The scene trains children to see their environment and current issues as powerful sources of visual ideas.

subject: B2 Creative Arts
altText: Basic 2 learners drawing quick sketches and short notes in simple sketchbooks or idea journals.
detailedDescription: Inside the classroom, each Basic 2 learner has a simple sketchbook or folded idea journal. On the pages they draw small, quick sketches of people, places and issues they have observed, adding short labels or words. The teacher moves between desks, asking what each drawing represents and encouraging learners to keep ideas for future artworks. The image shows children building a bank of visual ideas instead of waiting passively for instructions.

subject: B2 Creative Arts
figureLabel: Experimenting with different visual art media
altText: Basic 2 pupils testing crayons, paint, collage papers and clay on shared tables in a classroom.
detailedDescription: In a Basic 2 classroom, groups of learners gather around low tables covered with drawing papers. On the tables are crayons, coloured pencils, watercolour paints, scraps of coloured paper, glue and a small amount of clay. Children experiment with lines, textures and colours, pressing, smudging and layering media while the teacher prompts them to notice differences and talk about which materials match their ideas best.

subject: B2 Creative Arts
figureLabel: Arranging shapes and sketches before making
altText: Basic 2 learners arranging cut-out shapes and rough sketches on larger paper to plan a composition.
detailedDescription: On the classroom floor and tables, Basic 2 learners place small cut-out pictures, coloured shapes and quick pencil sketches onto larger sheets of paper. They move pieces around while discussing which arrangement tells their story best. Some work alone, others in pairs, while the teacher reminds them to consider balance, space and focal point before gluing or drawing the final work.

subject: B2 Creative Arts
figureLabel: Creating an idea board for artworks
altText: A Basic 2 classroom idea board filled with sketches, colour tests and short notes about planned artworks.
detailedDescription: On a wall in the Basic 2 classroom, a large manila-sheet idea board is covered with small sketches, colour swatches and notes. Learners stand in front of the board, pointing to images that match the artworks they are planning. The teacher helps them link their sketches and notes on the board to the choices they will make about media, colour and composition in their final pieces.

subject: B2 Creative Arts
figureLabel: Moving from sketch to finished artwork
altText: Basic 2 learner showing a page of rough sketches, a clearer plan and a finished coloured artwork on a desk.
detailedDescription: On a single desk, three stages of one learner’s work are shown: a rough page of doodles, a clearer sketch of the chosen idea and a larger, coloured artwork. The child proudly points to the finished piece while a classmate compares it with the earlier sketches. The teacher highlights the importance of planning, revising and improving ideas before finalising an artwork.

subject: B2 Creative Arts
figureLabel: Exhibition on history and culture of other communities
altText: Basic 2 learners exhibiting artworks about another Ghanaian community’s history and culture to classmates and parents.
detailedDescription: A Basic 2 classroom has been turned into a small exhibition. On the walls and tables are drawings and paintings showing festivals, chiefs, elders, traders and special cultural activities from another Ghanaian community. Learners stand beside their artworks, explaining them to visiting classmates and a few parents. Simple handwritten labels show the artist’s name, title and community represented.

subject: B2 Creative Arts
figureLabel: Exhibition on natural and manmade environments in other places
altText: Basic 2 pupils guiding visitors through artworks showing rivers, farms, markets and buildings from another Ghanaian community.
detailedDescription: In the same classroom gallery, another section of the display shows paintings and drawings of mountains, rivers, farms, bridges, markets and special buildings from another part of Ghana. Basic 2 pupils act as guides, pointing out features and reading short captions to visitors. The exhibition title at the top reads ‘Our Friends’ Environment in Another Region’.

subject: B2 Creative Arts
figureLabel: Exhibition on topical issues in other communities
altText: Basic 2 class exhibiting posters about flooding, sanitation, road safety and other issues in other Ghanaian communities.
detailedDescription: Another part of the Basic 2 exhibition shows posters and drawings about topical issues affecting other Ghanaian communities, such as flooding, dirty gutters, unsafe crossing and bushfires. Learners explain how their posters show both the problems and suggested solutions. A simple feedback chart allows visitors to mark what they learned or which artwork they found most powerful.

subject: B2 Creative Arts
figureLabel: Using guidelines to view and respond to artworks
altText: Basic 2 pupils sitting in a semicircle, using a classroom guideline chart to talk about how an artwork makes them feel.
detailedDescription: Basic 2 learners sit in a semicircle facing a display of artworks. Next to the display is a large chart listing simple guidelines such as ‘Look quietly first’, ‘Say what you see’, ‘Say how you feel’, and ‘Respect others’ work’. One child stands and uses the guide to talk about a selected painting while others listen and raise their hands to respond.

subject: B2 Creative Arts
figureLabel: Using questions to assess and derive meaning
altText: Basic 2 learners in small groups using a question guide on the board to discuss the message of an artwork.
detailedDescription: After viewing artworks, Basic 2 learners sit in small groups with one artwork on each table. On the board, a question guide asks: ‘What is happening?’, ‘What message is this artwork giving?’, ‘What do you like and why?’. Learners point to parts of the picture and discuss, while a group secretory writes short notes. Later, groups share their interpretations with the whole class.
